newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine January deficit seen at $400 million.
newsitem.headline: Argentine January deficit seen at $400 million.

text.p: Argentina will have a central government deficit of around $400 million in January, in line with targets agreed with the International Monetary Fund, finance secretary Pablo Guidotti said Thursday.

"The deficit will be in line with our agreement with the IMF. A deficit of $1.04 billion is slated for the first quarter and the deficit in January will be around $400 million," Guidotti told reporters.
Argentina has agreed on a deficit of $3.0 billion for all of 1997 with the IMF.
Guidotti added that in the first half of March an IMF team will visit Argentina to negotiate a new extended fund facility.
"The most important thing will be to extend the time scale of the IMF program and fix additional structural reforms," Guidotti said.
He added that January tax collection that came in at $4.36 billion "was good, and was within our forecasts."
"We do not have to be euphoric about this figure. Tax collections were slightly higher than what we had projected and agreed with the IMF," he said.
The official added that the government is studying the possibility of eliminating exemptions on revenue tax on exports.
